subtitle: Conflict styles differ in directness and emotional expression. Explore those differences without turning a public model into a personal score or a group script.
scope: For staff across DHS. Selected public explanations of Mitchell Hammer’s Intercultural Conflict Style model support original adult learning cases and private reflection. This course does not administer the ICS Inventory, reproduce its questions, issue a profile, assign an IDI orientation or rank people. Actual conduct, agency responsibilities and formal processes remain. Native American and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA. Participation in this learning is voluntary.
introTranscript: People may approach a substantive disagreement through explicit words or contextual messages, and may express or restrain emotion in different ways. Learn the two dimensions and four named combinations in Hammer’s public conflict-style model. Then explore personally meanings the people describe and a response that changes through understanding, with room for private growth and actual responsibilities.

intro.heading: Understand the two dimensions before using a style name
intro.body:
Mitchell Hammer’s public Intercultural Conflict Style model combines two dimensions: direct or indirect approaches to communicating a substantive disagreement, and emotionally restrained or expressive approaches to dealing with emotional upset. They answer different questions. A person can state a concern explicitly while expressing strong feeling, or state it explicitly with controlled outward emotion. Directness is not automatically the same as visible intensity.

The public names are Discussion for direct and restrained, Engagement for direct and expressive, Accommodation for indirect and restrained, and Dynamic for indirect and expressive. These names identify combinations in this particular model. They are not four steps of an IDI continuum or a ranking from less to more important. Accommodation here is a conflict-style name, not the employment accommodation process and not a requirement to surrender a concern.

In this course, supplied message descriptions help you learn the distinctions. They do not provide the information or process needed to assess a person’s core pattern. The official ICS Inventory is a separate instrument with its own questions and profile; neither is reproduced here. You are not asked to type a colleague, award a score or assign yourself a fixed label.

A useful beginning is to consider which question you are answering: how the issue is communicated, how feeling is expressed, or what you have inferred about the person. Private reflection can help you recognize a familiar interpretation without submitting a personal conflict account. The practice descriptions are an equally valid way to learn the model.

flashcards.back: In the public model, an approach that communicates the substantive disagreement through explicit verbal statements.
In the public model, an approach that communicates the disagreement through context, relational cues or less explicit messages.
In the public model, more visible expression of emotional upset; it is distinct from a finding about disrespectful conduct.
In the public model, more controlled outward expression during emotional upset; it does not prove agreement or absence of feeling.
A named pairing of the two dimensions in the public model, rather than a rank of importance or a diagnosis from one exchange.

items.title: Read the issue and emotion as different dimensions
items.body: A direct statement of the concern can be emotionally restrained or expressive. Combining those questions too early can make every emphatic statement seem direct and every quiet one indirect. The public model instead keeps the substance and outward emotional approach distinct before naming a combination.

items.title: Learn the names within the particular model
items.body: Discussion and Engagement share directness but differ in emotional approach. Accommodation and Dynamic share indirectness but differ in emotional approach. The labels are meaningful through those pairings, rather than through everyday assumptions that accommodation means yielding or dynamic means better performance.

items.title: Do not turn a description into a personal profile
items.body: An educational message description can demonstrate a dimension. It does not establish an individual’s usual approach across contexts or a formal inventory result. Recognizing this limit lets you learn useful concepts without creating a colleague’s record, an assessment score or a rank of intercultural development.

tabs.label: Directness and intensity are collapsed
tabs.body: A reader calls every strongly felt message direct and every quiet message indirect. That confuses the two questions and makes the four combinations harder to understand. A quiet statement may name the issue explicitly, while an expressive message may communicate it through context or a story.

tabs.label: Style names become an importance ladder
tabs.body: A reader assumes Dynamic is the highest level because its everyday name sounds energetic. The model supplies combinations, not a developmental ranking. Learning all four can widen understanding without claiming that one name describes a more valuable person or an advanced IDI orientation.

tabs.label: Dimensions and learning purpose stay distinct
tabs.body: The reader first identifies the described issue approach and emotional approach, then uses the correct public combination name. This supports concept learning while keeping the separate inventory and personal profile outside the exercise. No disclosure, colleague classification or required work measure is needed.

check.question: Which statement accurately describes the public model?
check.correct: It combines direct or indirect issue communication with emotionally restrained or expressive approaches; its four names are combinations rather than ranks.
wrong: Directness and emotional expressiveness are the same dimension.
Dynamic is the most advanced IDI orientation in the model.
A single course answer establishes a person’s official ICS profile.
check.feedbackCorrect: The answer keeps the two dimensions, named combinations and learning-versus-assessment distinction accurate.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Directness concerns the substantive message, while emotional approach is a different dimension. Dynamic is a combination here rather than an IDI orientation or superior rank. A course answer does not establish an official ICS profile. Learn the public distinctions without collapsing them or turning practice into personal assessment.

items.text: Direct communication states the substantive concern explicitly.

Restraint describes more controlled outward feeling during upset.
A style name determines a person’s importance.

image.caption: A person writes on a whiteboard while people at a long table look toward it.

intro.heading: Hear direct and indirect messages without equating them with honesty
intro.body:
In a practice volunteer workshop, Sora and Levi disagree about whether newcomers should practice a repair before watching the full demonstration. Sora says, “I want the first practice before the full demonstration.” Levi tells a story about an earlier shared workshop where watching together helped people begin without feeling singled out. Sora initially hears a failure to answer; Levi initially hears Sora’s statement as setting the relationship aside. The substantive sequence is still in question.

Sora supplies a personally learned meaning from an astronomy club: naming the particular point of disagreement showed responsibility for a problem that others could help solve. Levi supplies a different meaning from a shared sewing circle: a relevant story invited people to consider the relationship without separating one person as the problem. Neither account represents all astronomy clubs or sewing circles. They explain what these messages mean to these people.

The public model’s direct dimension helps notice Sora’s explicit statement; its indirect dimension helps notice Levi’s contextual approach. Those observations do not decide honesty, intelligence or a formal style profile. Asking Levi which sequence the story supports can make the concern clearer. Asking Sora what the first practice is intended to accomplish can bring the reason into the exchange. Clarifying either message is different from demanding that a person adopt a universal communication rule.

You can privately examine an assumption that explicit words are always honest or contextual words are always evasive, or use the example. An explanation can become clearer without assigning a population script or rejecting a meaningful relationship concern. The next sequence and its suitability are not yet agreed.

items.title: An explicit concern can make the issue identifiable
items.body: Sora states the preferred sequence directly. That helps Levi identify the disputed point, but does not make Sora’s option automatically suitable or prove that all other approaches are evasive. Asking for the purpose of the first practice adds relevant meaning while keeping the substantive choice open.

items.title: A contextual concern can have a substantive point
items.body: Levi’s story draws attention to shared preparation and not singling someone out. Sora can ask which sequence Levi is proposing instead of deciding there is no concern. The question seeks the point of the message while retaining its relationship meaning; it does not require a cultural biography.

items.title: The personal account can widen the interpretation
items.body: Sora can hear an invitation to consider the relationship; Levi can hear responsibility to a solvable point. These shifts come from the supplied accounts, not from typing the speakers. Both can keep their own values and examine the sequence without treating understanding as automatic agreement or a completed workshop plan.

tabs.label: Directness is treated as proof of honesty
tabs.body: Sora’s explicit statement is declared the only trustworthy contribution. That may make Levi’s actual concern harder to hear and adds a moral judgment the words cannot establish. An explicit message can help identify an issue without proving that a different approach is deceptive.

tabs.label: Indirectness is treated as proof of evasion
tabs.body: Levi’s story is dismissed as refusal before Sora asks about its point. The supplied meaning concerns shared preparation, rather than no interest in the decision. A clarification can make the proposed sequence identifiable while keeping that meaning, without declaring all contextual messages good or every story relevant.

tabs.label: The concern and meaning are clarified together
tabs.body: The two ask what each message supports and why it matters. Sora’s explicit point and Levi’s contextual story can become understandable without forcing a fixed label or agreeing on the sequence. This applies the public distinction while learning remains separate from an official personal profile.

check.question: Which inquiry best fits Levi’s contextual message?
check.correct: Ask which sequence the story supports and why shared preparation matters, without deciding that indirectness proves evasion.
wrong: Declare that every contextual message is dishonest.
Treat Sora’s explicit preference as automatic authority over the workshop.
Require Levi to explain an entire community before the concern is heard.
check.feedbackCorrect: The inquiry makes the substantive concern clearer while respecting the particular supplied meaning.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A contextual message does not establish dishonesty. Sora’s explicit preference does not confer decision authority. A community explanation would demand information unrelated to the particular concern. Ask what the story supports and why it matters, while leaving the actual sequence and formal personal profile unassigned.

items.text: Sora explicitly names a first-practice preference.
Levi’s story concerns shared preparation without singling someone out.
Ask which sequence Levi’s story supports.
Ask what Sora’s first practice is intended to accomplish.

lessons.statement: Hear the concern and the person’s meaning rather than treating emotional display as the verdict.

image.caption: A person writes on a whiteboard while people at a long table look toward it.

intro.heading: Hear emotional expression and restraint without inferring sincerity
intro.body:
A separate original workshop example keeps the issue communication explicit. Fen says with visible emotion, “I am upset that the preparation time was removed.” Pia states the same concern with a measured outward response. Both name the issue directly. Their outward emotional approaches differ; neither display alone establishes how much the person cares, whether the concern is accurate or a formal assessed style.

Fen supplies a particular account from family music gatherings: letting others hear the feeling showed sincere commitment to working through a disagreement. Pia supplies an account from library-volunteer review conversations: a measured response made room to hear the concern without crowding another person’s attention. Pia initially hears Fen’s intensity as disregard; Fen initially hears Pia’s restraint as lack of commitment. The new accounts give each another possible interpretation.

Pia can ask about the concern without demanding that Fen first prove sincerity through calmness. Fen can hear the measured response as considered attention rather than agreement or indifference. Both can state what the changed preparation means and how to continue. The course does not prescribe the same display for every setting, require a reader to perform emotion or decide that the proposed preparation change is settled.

Actual conduct still matters. Emotional expressiveness is not a blanket permission for threats, harassment or intimidation, and restraint is not proof that an exchange was respectful. The Council of Europe distinguishes respect for people from accepting actions that violate rights. Privately examine a meaning you associate with visible or measured feeling, or use the example; the learning need not become a recorded conflict or personality judgment.

items.title: The explicit issue can stay the same
items.body: Fen and Pia both directly name the preparation concern. That makes it possible to examine emotional approach without changing the substantive communication dimension. It also prevents a reader from calling every restrained response indirect or every expressive response more accurate merely because of its display.

items.title: A supplied meaning can change a first judgment
items.body: Fen explains sincere commitment; Pia explains room for attention. These accounts widen the first interpretations of disregard and indifference. They do not describe every family gathering or library volunteer, and they do not establish that the actual preparation issue is correct or already resolved.

items.title: Meaning and actual conduct are both relevant
items.body: Hearing sincerity in Fen’s account is different from excusing prohibited behavior. Hearing care in Pia’s account is different from proving every quiet exchange respectful. A response can hear the particular concern and learned meaning while keeping actual conduct, choice and any formal responsibility visible.

tabs.label: More feeling is called more commitment
tabs.body: Fen’s visible emotion is treated as proof of greater sincerity and Pia’s restraint is dismissed as indifference. Display alone cannot establish either conclusion. Pia’s supplied meaning provides a reason for the measured response, while the actual preparation concern remains something to examine rather than score.

tabs.label: Less feeling is called greater competence
tabs.body: Pia’s measured expression is treated as the only competent approach and Fen’s intensity as a personal flaw. That makes one display the universal standard. Hearing Fen’s account can widen interpretation without ignoring actual conduct or treating every expressive response as suitable in every context.

tabs.label: The account informs how the concern is heard
tabs.body: Both explicit concerns remain visible, and each person hears another meaning of care. The response can change without a fixed profile or demanded emotional performance. Practical preparation questions and actual conduct limits remain, while private self-understanding is valuable even without a workshop decision.

check.question: Which interpretation fits the two accounts?
check.correct: Both name the issue directly; their different outward emotional approaches have personally meanings the people describe that do not prove sincerity, agreement or a formal style.
wrong: Pia’s restraint proves complete agreement with the change.
Fen’s visible emotion proves greater competence in every setting.
A learned expressive meaning excuses any threatening conduct.
check.feedbackCorrect: The interpretation separates the issue, outward emotion, particular meaning and actual limits.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Restraint does not prove agreement or absence of feeling. Visible emotion does not establish competence across settings. A learned meaning cannot excuse threats or prohibited conduct. Hear the explicit concern and the person’s account without making display a personal verdict or erasing actual responsibilities.

items.text: Both directly name the removed preparation time.
Pia links a measured response with room for attention.
Fen initially hears restraint as lack of commitment.
Pia initially hears intensity as disregard.
A quiet response proves complete agreement.
Expressiveness excuses threats.

intro.heading: Use the four combinations accurately as learning concepts
intro.body:
Return to the public names after separating the two dimensions. Discussion combines direct issue communication and emotional restraint. Engagement combines direct issue communication and emotional expressiveness. Accommodation combines indirect issue communication and emotional restraint. Dynamic combines indirect issue communication and emotional expressiveness. The chart on the model owner’s public page supports those pairings.

Four practice teaching cards state their features explicitly. Card A directly names an issue with controlled outward emotion. Card B directly names an issue with expressive outward feeling. Card C communicates through contextual messages with controlled outward emotion. Card D communicates through contextual messages with expressive outward feeling. Matching the cards to Discussion, Engagement, Accommodation and Dynamic retrieves the definitions; it does not infer hidden meanings from a real person.

Everyday associations can make a label misleading. Discussion does not mean the only style that talks; Engagement does not mean everyone else lacks commitment. Accommodation is a name in this model, not necessarily yielding and not an ADA request. Dynamic is not a higher stage. None of these names should be mapped onto a person’s IDI orientation or applied to an entire population from a group label.

You can privately practice the matching or explain why an inaccurate pairing is wrong. The official inventory, scoring and interpretive profile remain separate and are not recreated. The learning is the public conceptual distinction and its use for better inquiry, not a credential, a personal record or a way to choose the most valuable colleague.

items.title: Compare the two direct combinations
items.body: Discussion and Engagement both use direct communication about the substantive issue. The difference in the public model is restrained versus expressive emotion. The teaching cards state those features, so matching is a definition exercise rather than a conclusion about a person’s underlying pattern or importance.

items.title: Compare the two indirect combinations
items.body: Accommodation and Dynamic both use indirect communication about the substantive issue. The difference is restrained versus expressive emotion. Learning those pairings prevents the everyday name Accommodation from being mistaken for automatic yielding, or Dynamic from being mistaken for a more advanced stage.

items.title: Keep the kind of conclusion accurate
items.body: A definition match can show that a reader remembers the public combinations. It cannot establish an official profile, national pattern, workplace suitability or assessed orientation. The exercise therefore uses supplied cards without requesting real conflict accounts or reconstructing proprietary inventory questions and scoring.

tabs.label: The direct pair
tabs.body: The card with explicit concern and restrained outward emotion illustrates Discussion; the card with explicit concern and expressive outward feeling illustrates Engagement. Neither card is a personal profile. Their shared directness makes the emotional distinction visible without implying that one approach is always better or more truthful.

tabs.label: The indirect pair
tabs.body: The card with contextual messages and restrained emotion illustrates Accommodation; the card with contextual messages and expressive feeling illustrates Dynamic. These are names in the particular public model. They do not establish automatic surrender, disability accommodation authority or a higher developmental level for the person who uses them.

tabs.label: Learning and formal assessment
tabs.body: The reader can retrieve the correct pairings and ask better questions about meaning. The official inventory and personal interpretation are separate. A score, assessed profile or group label does not emerge from these cards, and course completion does not rank people by conflict style or IDI development.

wrong: Discussion: indirect/expressive; Engagement: indirect/restrained; Accommodation: direct/expressive; Dynamic: direct/restrained.
All four names describe the same combination and different levels of importance.
Accommodation is an ADA procedure and Dynamic is an advanced IDI orientation.
check.feedbackCorrect: The set accurately combines the two public dimensions without adding another framework or an importance rank.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Reversing the pairings misstates the public model. The four names identify different combinations rather than levels of importance. Accommodation here is not an ADA procedure, and Dynamic is not an IDI orientation. Retrieve the actual two dimensions while keeping educational matching separate from an official personal profile.

lessons.statement: Change the approach through meaning without requiring a person to become a style label.

image.caption: A person writes on a whiteboard while people at a long table look toward it.

intro.heading: Bridge an approach while retaining the concern and actual duties
intro.body:
Sora now asks Levi, “What does the earlier workshop suggest we should do first, and what would that protect?” Levi explains the shared-preparation concern and asks what Sora’s first practice is intended to make possible. Their responses change because the personally meanings the people describe are clearer. Neither needs to prove that one is a fixed Discussion or Accommodation person. The rehearsal sequence remains an actual question.

In the separate Fen and Pia example, Pia acknowledges the sincerity meaning of visible feeling and asks about the lost preparation. Fen recognizes considered attention in Pia’s measured response. They can choose a way to continue that hears the concern without demanding an emotional performance, forced calmness as a credibility test or compulsory expressive disclosure. No preparation arrangement or relationship repair is yet confirmed.

In suitable DHS work, staff can use these distinctions to ask better questions while keeping responsibility for their work. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, leadership, knowledge and feedback. Support develops staff capability rather than doing every inquiry for them or creating a universal review gate. Applicable formal analysis and agency processes remain rather than being completed by a style discussion.

A separate practice allegation concerns protected conduct, not merely different approaches. A staff member tells manager Rowan that a coworker repeatedly mocked the staff member’s national origin. Under MMB Policy 1436, managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow assigned agency procedures. Rowan does not use a style name to excuse the conduct, delay a report or decide the allegation. Actual authorized investigation responsibilities remain; this course neither replaces nor removes them.

items.title: Clarify the concern in a meaning-sensitive way
items.body: Sora asks what Levi’s story supports and protects instead of requiring a directness test. Levi asks about Sora’s intended result instead of treating explicitness as relationship rejection. These responses retain both concerns and personally meanings the people describe while the suitable sequence remains open rather than automatically agreed.

items.title: Invite a suitable approach rather than a new personality
items.body: Fen and Pia can hear each account and choose how to continue. That is different from demanding that someone display stronger emotion or become restrained to prove competence. The actual concern and conduct limits remain, and no style label decides which preparation arrangement is feasible.

items.title: Follow the separate required response
items.body: Rowan’s national-origin allegation engages the manager’s immediate all-allegation reporting duty to HR or agency AAO under Policy 1436. A cultural approach is not a defense or reporting gate. Actual assigned procedures and investigation duties apply while the course makes no legal or personnel finding.

tabs.label: A preferred style is imposed
tabs.body: The coordinator requires every participant to become direct and restrained before any concern is heard. That turns a model distinction into a universal credibility test. A useful response can seek understandable concerns and appropriate conduct without forced style conversion or dismissing a personally supplied meaning.

tabs.label: A style name excuses a protected-class allegation
tabs.body: Rowan calls national-origin mockery expressive and decides no report is needed. That substitutes a model label for an actual formal duty. Understanding style does not excuse prohibited conduct, decide an allegation or delay the immediate HR or agency AAO report required of managers and supervisors.

tabs.label: Meaning informs response and duties remain
tabs.body: The workshop participants clarify the concern and choose an approach without a personal profile. Separately, Rowan follows immediate reporting and assigned procedures. This keeps useful intercultural learning connected to practice while actual authority, formal processes and the unconfirmed result remain distinct.

check.feedbackCorrect: The description supports meaning-informed practice without a style test or substitution for actual duties.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A preferred style cannot become a credibility or participation gate. A model label does not excuse protected-class conduct or replace immediate manager reporting. A learning discussion does not complete formal analysis or investigation. Retain the actual issue, choice, authority and agency procedures while using meaning to improve the response.

intro.heading: Reflect on patterns without making a permanent type
intro.body:
The example supplies limited follow-up. Sora now understands Levi’s story as a concern about shared preparation, and Levi now understands Sora’s explicit point as responsibility to a solvable issue. Fen and Pia describe their different meanings of care more clearly. The workshop sequence, restored preparation and longer-term effect are not supplied as completed results. These particular shifts can be recognized without claiming universal agreement or successful conflict resolution.

A reader may also privately recognize an interpretation that has felt automatic: explicit words as the only honest approach, visible feeling as the only sincerity, or restraint as the only competence. Noticing another personally supplied meaning can widen self-understanding. It need not produce a permanent personal type, a score, a coworker record or a public reflection. The practice accounts are available when a personal example is not wanted.

Hammer’s historical conceptual discussion emphasizes meaning in context and the capacity to adapt responses across situations. The Council of Europe likewise describes personalized cultural affiliations and the value of self-understanding. These concepts support thoughtful reflection rather than assigning one exchange as proof of someone’s core style. The formal inventory and profile are not recreated by a course closing question.

In actual work, practical follow-through needs the relevant information, choices and responsibilities. A revised interpretation is not proof that a service outcome improved, a concern disappeared or required analysis was completed. Use the job aid to keep the model’s definitions, personal meaning, actual conduct and remaining questions visible. Personal growth can be meaningful while suitable practical work continues through its real roles.

items.title: Name the actual learning rather than a universal repair
items.body: Sora and Levi describe wider interpretations; Fen and Pia describe clearer meanings of care. Those are particular changes supplied by the example. They do not prove every participant agrees, the sequence is decided or all preparation concerns are resolved. Naming the actual shifts preserves their value without an invented result.

items.title: Reflect on meaning rather than assign a permanent type
items.body: A reader can notice a familiar interpretation and consider another meaning privately. That is different from deciding a fixed core style from one exchange. The model’s distinctions can support self-understanding while context, changing responses and the separate formal inventory remain relevant.

items.title: Let personal growth and practical work both matter
items.body: A private insight can be worthwhile without a measurable work product. When actual decisions need follow-through, their information and responsibilities also remain. Neither purpose must erase the other, and a course closing does not establish an individual assessment, completed complaint process or universal service result.

tabs.label: One exchange becomes a permanent label
tabs.body: The reader decides a person is always Dynamic or Discussion from one visible response. That bypasses meaning, context and the separate inventory. A supplied message feature can illustrate a definition without proving a person’s usual approach, orientation, importance or capacity to adapt.

tabs.label: Insight is dismissed without a work score
tabs.body: The reader rejects a wider understanding because no workplace metric changed. That makes personal growth subordinate to a result the example does not supply. Understanding a learned interpretation can be meaningful privately, alongside suitable actual work and without disclosure or an assessed cultural rank.

tabs.label: Specific learning and open results remain distinct
tabs.body: The reader names the two dimensions, correct combinations and particular meaning-informed shifts, then leaves the workshop decisions and broader effects open. This preserves the learning without permanent typing or false reassurance. Actual follow-through can continue through real choices, evidence and responsibilities.

jobAid.title: Use conflict-style concepts without typing people
jobAid.subtitle: Keep issue communication, outward emotion, personal meaning and actual responsibility distinct.
jobAid.intro: Use private reflection, the supplied teaching cards or appropriate actual inquiry. This is not the ICS Inventory, a profile report, an IDI assessment or a conflict-resolution credential.

sections.heading: Understand the public combinations
items: Separate direct or indirect communication about the issue from expressive or restrained outward emotion.
Discussion is direct/restrained; Engagement is direct/expressive.
Accommodation is indirect/restrained; Dynamic is indirect/expressive.
The four combinations are not levels of importance, an IDI progression or an employment accommodation procedure.

sections.heading: Hear particular meanings before judging
items: Ask what the explicit point or contextual message supports and why it matters.
Do not make directness synonymous with honesty or indirectness with evasion.
Do not infer sincerity, competence, agreement or absence of feeling from outward emotion alone.
Use personally meanings the people describe to widen interpretation without a group script or a demanded biography.
A private insight or practice reflection can remain unrecorded and meaningful without a work score.

sections.heading: Apply learning with actual limits
items: Let clarified meaning change the response while keeping the substantive concern and genuine choice.
A proposed way to continue does not prove an agreed sequence, restored preparation or repaired relationship.
Staff retain their work and can seek the consultant’s guidance and feedback without a universal gate.
Keep actual agency processes, authority and formal-analysis responsibilities separate from a learning discussion.
Name specific understanding and unanswered questions without permanent profiles or universal results.

remember: The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and supports staff capability through guidance, leadership, knowledge and feedback.
Managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer under Policy 1436 and follow actual assigned procedures.
An expressive or restrained account does not excuse prohibited conduct or remove actual authorized investigation responsibilities.
The formal ICS Inventory and its questions, scoring and personal profile are not reproduced; one exchange does not give an official result.
Personal growth stands alongside practical application; reflection does not require disclosure, a coworker record or live work proof.

sources.title: ICS Inventory: Public Intercultural Conflict Style model
sources.note: The model owner’s public two dimensions and four named combinations. Commercial claims, usage counts, questionnaire items and profile scoring are not reproduced. This course uses original learning examples rather than administering the inventory.

sources.title: Mitchell Hammer: Solving problems and resolving conflict using the Intercultural Conflict Style model and inventory
sources.note: Selected historical conceptual sections on the two dimensions, meanings in context, capacity to adapt and named combinations. National and ethnic exemplars, instrument questions, scoring and historical usage statistics are not used as personal predictions or course assessment.

sources.title: Council of Europe: Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Personalized and internally varied cultural meanings, multiple perspectives, self-understanding and limits of accepting harmful actions. Original cases do not assign assessed orientations or group styles.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1436: Harassment and Discrimination Prohibited
sources.note: Actual immediate manager and supervisor reporting of all protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or agency Affirmative Action Officer, assigned procedures and non-retaliation. A style explanation does not decide an allegation or replace reporting.

sources.title: DHS Equity Policy
sources.note: Actual daily-work and relevant formal-analysis responsibilities remain separate from learning the public model. Course practice is not a completed analysis or new program decision authority.
